# Benchmark: the same requests with and without the skill

<!-- generated by benchmarks/page.py from benchmarks/results/*.json; do not edit -->

Each request is given to a model in an agent loop with one tool (`bash`) and a limit of 20 calls. With the skill, SKILL.md is in the system prompt and the tools are on disk; without it, the model has ffmpeg and ffprobe. Every output file is measured (length, frame, streams, loudness, a frame's brightness, the pitch of the sound); what the model says it did is recorded and never graded. The models are reached through an API, not run on local hardware.

Read a difference of one or two correct answers as noise when a cell ran once (`Runs per task` 1). A figure the source did not state is `not measured`, never a zero.

Per model, calls per request went 11.5 to 9.0, 8.9 to 5.5 and 7.9 to 5.0 against 4.4.0; #670 does not say which model is which beyond what #684 gives.
- DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, skill, 4.4.1: #684, the one model of the three that uses more calls with the skill. Its correct count was not published.
- DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, raw, none (beside 4.4.1): #684: "7.8 calls per request without the skill, 9.0 with it (4.4.1), while the other two models use fewer with the skill". Its correct count was not published.

## Running it

One command per model and arm; the endpoint and key come from the environment and are never written to a file:

```
export BENCH_API_URL=https://<provider>/v1/chat/completions BENCH_API_KEY=...
python3 benchmarks/run.py MODEL --arm skill --runs 3
python3 benchmarks/run.py MODEL --arm raw --runs 3
python3 benchmarks/page.py --write
```

`--dry-run` prints the tasks and the request each would send, with no endpoint and no network. `--only cut,mute` runs part of the set; `--budget 5` stops starting runs after five dollars. Each run's transcript is kept under `--out`. The model's commands run in bash, so a run needs Linux or macOS (WSL on Windows); `--dry-run` works anywhere. After a release, the `benchmark` workflow (Actions, run by hand) does the same on a runner and attaches the results file; committing it updates this page. The checkers are tested with a known-good and a known-bad output for every task (`tests/test_benchmarks.py`).
